# Knowledge Audit

## Purpose
Assess the state of the Knowledge department in the whole system: how well documentation, decision history, operating reports, and reusable workflows hold together, and where they are weak.

## Scope
- Documentation, kept current with the work
- Decision history, with reasons
- Operating reports the founder can read without extra context
- Reusable workflows
- Memory that links decisions, milestones, and learnings

## What is in place
- [ ] Lead agents for docs and knowledge are named and active
- [ ] Skill that keeps docs current with the code
- [ ] Skill that writes notes in clean markdown
- [ ] Workflow that records decisions with reasons
- [ ] Workflow that turns milestones into summaries
- [ ] Report templates the founder can read without extra context
- [ ] Knowledge base that links decisions, milestones, and learnings

## Gaps
- [ ] Docs lag behind the code
- [ ] Decisions are made in chat and lost
- [ ] Reports differ in shape from one department to the next
- [ ] Milestones and learnings are not linked to decisions
- [ ] Knowledge capture is manual and inconsistent
- [ ] Nobody can audit company state from the knowledge base alone

## Next steps
- Pick the highest priority gap and name its owner
- Add or fix the missing agent, skill, command, or workflow for that gap
- Run the new piece on a real decision or report and check the result against evidence
- Record the decision and the outcome in the decision log
- Repeat for the next gap
- Share the finished audit and the changes with the people who need them, so the work reaches distribution
